newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pacific Dunlop sees unchanged gearing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pacific Dunlop sees unchanged gearing.

text.p: Industrial conglomerate Pacific Dunlop ltd said on Friday that its gearing stood at 158 percent at the end of June and that it did not see that changing dramatically in the near term.
"We don't see that changing dramatically over the next six months or so," Pacific Dunlop executive general manager of finance Philip Gay told reporters.
The group's gearing has averaged aRound 145 percent in recent years, Group Managing Director Rod Chadwick said, adding that the correct gearing was somewhere between 125 and 150 percent.
Pacific Dunlop's gearing stood at 170 percent at June 30, 1995.
Earlier, Pacific Dunlop reported a net loss of A$132.74 million for 1995/96, versus 1994/95's A$94.2 million net profit.

This included abnormal losses before tax of A$284.55 million, linked mostly to the troubled Telectronics heart pacemaker group, compared with an abnormal loss before tax of A$197.29 million the previous year.
